subject: [PATCH v4 04/19] selftests/mm: skip khugepaged page cache cases without a PMD folio

reviews.author: Lorenzo Stoakes (ARM)
reviews.summary: Raised concerns about the comment being too verbose and suggested trimming it. Also questioned whether the patch is inferring file-backed khugepaged behavior from shmem.

reviews.author: Mike Rapoport (Microsoft)
reviews.summary: Provided a minor nitpick about the wording of the comment, suggesting it be rephrased to match the code. Also added a Reviewed-by tag.

2026-08-15.patch_summary: This patch series modifies the khugepaged selftest to skip certain page cache cases where a PMD-sized folio is not supported due to limitations in MAX_PAGECACHE_ORDER on arm64 architectures.

reviews.author: Mike Rapoport
reviews.summary:
Reviewer suggested a more precise wording in the code comment to match the kernel's behavior, recommending 'kernel refuses these collapses' instead of 'the kernel refuses these collapses by design'.

Gave Reviewed-by
reviews.raw_body:
Nit: the code comment phrases it better: "so kernel refuses these
collapses".

2026-08-20.patch_summary: This patch modifies the khugepaged selftest to skip cases involving page cache folios that are larger than the PMD order, which is not supported on certain architectures. The issue arises because the page cache caps folio order at MAX_PAGECACHE_ORDER, which is smaller than the PMD order on arm64 with 64K pages. As a result, the kernel refuses to collapse these large folios and the test fails. To fix this, the patch adds checks to skip these cases when running the selftest.

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: The author is addressing a concern about the naming of `thp_shmem_supported_orders()` and its relation to page cache capabilities, explaining that it's actually checking for regular file support as well. The author plans to add a new function `thp_file_supported_orders()` to clarify this.
reviews.raw_body:
The helper is named after shmem but the sysfs set is the page cache one.
`thpsize_create()` creates the per-order `shmem_enabled` attribute under one
condition:

	if (BIT(order) & THP_ORDERS_ALL_FILE_DEFAULT) {

and that mask is orders 1 to `MAX_PAGECACHE_ORDER`.

So hugepages-<N>kB/shmem_enabled exists means "the page cache can hold an
order-N folio", for regular files as much as for shmem.

thp_shmem_supported_orders() name is confusing. I think, I will add
`thp_file_supported_orders()` over the same sysfs walk and use that
here.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov
